merger_description:
EQT Fund Management S.à r.l., through a wholly owned special purpose vehicle, Elevate BidCo GmbH (part of the investment fund EQT X), proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Exolaunch GmbH (together with its subsidiaries, **Exolaunch**) (the **Acquisition**).

EQT X is a private investment fund controlled by EQT Fund Management S.à r.l., an alternative investment fund manager.

Exolaunch, headquartered in Berlin (Germany), manufactures and supplies satellite deployment hardware, facilitating the integration and aggregation of a wide range of satellites with different launch vehicles, deploying payloads into their target orbits. Exolaunch also provides related satellite launch mission management and deployment services, providing end-to-end launch services including mission design, satellite testing, launch capacity procurement, integration of satellites to launch vehicles, and deployment into orbit. Exolaunch operates through wholly owned subsidiaries in the USA, France and Japan. Exolaunch is currently solely controlled by its founder Dmitriy Sternharz.

determination_table_content.details:
EQT Fund Management S.à r.l. (EQT), through a wholly owned
special purpose vehicle Elevate BidCo GmbH (Elevate), applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the shares in Exolaunch GmbH (together with its subsidiaries,
Exolaunch), as described in the transaction documents provided as
part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Elevate, is a special purpose vehicle established for
and in connection with the acquisition. Elevate is wholly owned by
EQT X, a private investment fund controlled by EQT, an alternative
investment fund manager.
The target, Exolaunch, is headquartered in Berlin, Germany, and
manufactures and supplies satellite deployment hardware,
facilitating the integration and aggregation of a wide range of
satellites with different launch vehicles, deploying payloads into their
target orbits. Exolaunch also provides related satellite launch
mission management and deployment services, providing end-to-end
launch services including mission design, satellite testing, launch
capacity procurement, integration of satellites to launch vehicles,
and deployment into orbit.
Exolaunch operates through wholly owned subsidiaries in the USA,
France and Japan.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. There is no horizontal or vertical overlap in
Australia between the acquirer (or its connected entities) and
Exolaunch in the supply of satellite deployment hardware, and
satellite launch mission management and deployment services.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
